content.caseIdentity: Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala, (2000) 6 SCC 359
content.holding: Laid down the doctrine of merger: dismissal of an SLP in limine does not attract the doctrine of merger, leaving the High Court order open to review, whereas disposal after leave merges the order into the Supreme Court decree.
content.relevance: Definitive authority on Article 136 stages and doctrine of merger.

evidence.note: Supreme Court of India (2000) 6 SCC 359; 2000 INSC 368; 2000 Supp (1) SCR 538; Doctrine of merger and Article 136 SLP dismissal effect.
